searchText: Killing refunds is an EIP: https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/3298 Yeah I think the biggest barriers to SC wallet adoption are (i) abstraction issues (can't put validation in the pre-gas-payment-commitment logic), and (ii) higher gas costs Of course, a solution to (i) would also greatly mitigate (ii) Do you want it discussed for London inclusion? If so, can you open a quick issue here: https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/ Done! Thanks! What fork would a SELFDESTRUCT behavior change be conceivably good for (I'm thinking replace the opcode's behavior with "send entire remaining balance to target as a call and do nothing else")? Shanghai? I also remember this channel had the idea of fixing the block number very early but making it reasonably far in the future why not disable selfdestruct outright? Because neutering it breaks less functionality, and I would also add that in the future a "send all" operation is a legitimate behavior For example, smart contract wallets post-EIP-1559 post-EIP-1559 you can't predict exactly what fee you'll pay, so the "neutered self-destruct as send-all" would help accounts full-clear their balance I'd argue it is a prerequisite for a verkle tree change, because any tree structure change becomes considerably simpler if we don't have to worry about the possibility of an arbitrary number of storage slots being zeroed out This argument puts me strongly in `SELFDESTRUCT => SENDALLETH` camp. we should *not* reuse the opcode imo What happens when execution hits the current opcode as it exists in contracts right now? Can you elaborate on what you mean by this?
